turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Not much. Work let me go a few weeks ago. It's fine though, gives me more time to sort out the thing with my neighbors.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand that losing your job can be tough, but I'm glad to see you today. Can you tell me more about the situation with your neighbors?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: They talk about me sometimes, through the wall, about what I'm doing, what I'm thinking. I don't really go into the kitchen at night anymore because that's when it's worst.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I can understand how that might be uncomfortable for you. Can you tell me more about the specific instances that make you feel this way?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, it's not just words, exactly... sometimes I hear them arguing, and it sounds like they're talking about me, but I'm not sure what they're saying. It's hard to make it out. And sometimes I'll be in bed, and I'll feel like they're staring at me from next door, even though I know it's not possible.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I appreciate you sharing this with me. It sounds like you're experiencing some auditory disturbances that are affecting your well-being. Can you tell me if there are any other symptoms or experiences related to this that you'd like to discuss?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's not just that. I feel like... sometimes I'll be walking down the street, and I'll see people, but it's like they're not really there. They're just kind of... floating or something. It's hard to explain.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's important that we address all your concerns. It sounds like you're experiencing some hallucinations. Can you tell me more about when these experiences occur and if there are any specific factors that seem to trigger them?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Look, I know what I see, okay? And it's not just me seeing things. I know what I hear, and I'm not crazy. I'm just... trying to live my life, but it's hard when it feels like everyone's watching me all the time.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand that this must be difficult for you. It's important to acknowledge your feelings and concerns. Can you tell me more about the support system you have in your life, if anyone that you feel comfortable talking to about what you're experiencing?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's hard to talk to anyone about this stuff. I've got a few friends, but they just don't get it. They think I'm paranoid or something. And my family... they just want me to "get over it". They don't understand.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand that it can be challenging to find support. It's important to have people around you who can empathize with your situation. Can you tell me if there are any other experiences or symptoms that you haven't shared yet? It's crucial to have a comprehensive understanding of your situation to provide the best support possible.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's just... sometimes I feel like I'm in a fog, you know? Like I'm going through the motions, but I'm not really living. And it's hard to get motivated to do anything, because it feels like nothing really matters.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you're experiencing a lack of motivation and a sense of detachment from your life. This can be a difficult time for many people. Can you tell me if there have been any recent changes in your life, or any stressors that might be contributing to these feelings?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: *sigh* Yeah... I guess losing my job was a big hit. And then my mom passed away a few months ago. I don't know, it's just all been a lot to deal with. But it's not just that. It's like... everything feels empty, you know? Like I'm just going through the motions, but there's no point to anything.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you've been through a difficult period in your life, with the loss of your job and your mother. It's normal to feel overwhelmed and struggle with motivation during these times. I'd like to ask you one last question: have you ever had thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation? It's important to discuss this if it's something you've experienced, so we can ensure your safety and well-being.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: *pauses, looking uncomfortable* No, nothing like that. I just feel... stuck, I guess. Like I'm just waiting for something to change, but I don't know what. *looks down, fidgeting with hands*

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's important to acknowledge that it's normal to feel stuck in difficult situations. It's crucial to focus on the present and work on finding ways to cope with your emotions and experiences. If you feel comfortable, we can end our session here. However, if you'd like to continue working on these issues together, I am here to help.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: *looks up, slightly relieved* Yeah, I think that's enough for today. Thanks for listening, I guess. *stands up, still looking a bit uncertain*

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Of course, it was my pleasure. Remember, it's important to reach out to your support system and not hesitate to seek professional help if you continue to feel overwhelmed. Take care.
